title: Finite Q3 cancellation-aware signed union-commutator audit
question: When the first-order Lie-Trotter commutator defect is grouped by exact union support and its signs are retained, do finite Q3 cancellations produce a cutoff-, beta-, volume- and source-uniform state-weighted coefficient?
method: Follow the hash-pinned EXP-001164 local-state Q3 fixture and rebuild every truncated oscillator, onsite term and bond term on volumes 2, 4 and 6 for cutoffs 3, 4, 5 and 6.
Group every overlapping pair commutator by its exact union support U, sum with the declared term-order sign, and explicitly rebuild the reverse term order to test antisymmetry.

For each signed group construct the induced H_U, normalized local Gibbs matrix rho_U at beta in {1/2,1,2}, and shifted K_U; evaluate raw, Gibbs and four-leg K_U^(1/2)-Gibbs seminorms for both the signed group and the corresponding absolute pair costs.
Check one full tensor embedding per volume, independently reconstruct all groups and aggregates, compare both lanes, and compile Lean R335 for exact signed cancellation and proxy bookkeeping.
finding: Primary 166/166 and independent 166/166 assertions pass over 36 volume/cutoff/beta rows; the integrated verifier passes 5743/5743 and Lean R335 compiles. Reverse-order groups are antisymmetric within the declared tolerance. Grouping retains finite cancellation: at the cutoff-6 endpoint the signed-to-absolute energy-weighted aggregate ratio is 0.7318002601630961 for beta=1/2, 0.7588370003593856 for beta=1 and 0.7740816491926341 for beta=2. The cancellation is incomplete: the signed energy-weighted sum per site still grows from cutoff 3 to 6 by ratios 7.975223006126479, 4.4727553658804275 and 2.1093674337122605 for beta=1/2,1 and 2, respectively, and the maximum signed weighted per-site value is 23.382788529134057. The same finite-grid ratios recur across the three graph volumes, while source-touching groups remain boundary-dependent. These observations do not establish a cutoff-, volume- or beta-uniform coefficient.
decision_reason: The signed union grouping demonstrates a real but partial cancellation relative to the absolute pair-sum proxy, so it is the appropriate finite diagnostic for a cancellation-aware Duhamel route. Because the signed weighted coefficient still grows strongly with cutoff on the declared grid, it cannot be promoted as a uniform replacement. The next proof obligation is analytic: derive cancellations before taking norms on a global-state-compatible common core, or prove a direct D,delta-D estimate; local finite Gibbs matrices alone cannot supply that transfer.
boundary: Finite oscillator matrices with inherited Q3 parameters, volumes 2, 4 and 6, cutoffs 3 through 6, beta in {1/2,1,2}, induced union Hamiltonians and listed source supports. No global KMS restriction, common unbounded domain, actual Trotter defect theorem, thermodynamic history, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or Clay conclusion follows.
next_action: Attempt an analytic global-state-compatible cancellation-aware D,delta-D estimate on the matching-layer common core, using the finite signed groups only as calibration; if uniformity fails, record the exact route obstruction before any common-alpha promotion.

adversarial_review.check: Signs are retained only within exact union-support groups and the absolute pair costs are reported separately.
The reverse term order is rebuilt and compared with the negative forward group matrix and all three seminorms.
rho_U is explicitly an induced finite Gibbs matrix and is not identified with an infinite-volume KMS restriction.
The four K_U^(1/2)-Gibbs legs are evaluated separately; no commutation of K_U, rho_U and the signed group is assumed.
Every declared row rebuilds all matrices and spectral factors; finite growth ratios are not asymptotic bounds.
Only declared source supports and exact union groups are aggregated, retaining boundary dependence.
R335 checks exact rational signed cancellation only; spectra, domains and QFT limits remain Python/open analysis.
Finite signed cancellation does not prove a global KMS state, common core, thermodynamic dynamics, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
